parsedVerdict.reasoning: All six files serve one concern: request and response DTOs for the curier controller. But they don't use the module's abstractions consistently. (1) The validation rule for the boolean field isActive is copied into two DTOs, and both copies use @IsString. UpdateOrderStatusDto validates its booleans with @IsBoolean, so the same rule lives in two places and both contradict the module's convention. (2) SavedCurierResponseDto.fromDomain fills a SavedCurierOrderResponseDto (orderDto), then returns orderReadonly (the domain entity's export) instead. This skips the module's own order response DTO and lets domain data reach the response. (3) The same method sets paymentDetails from commissionRate, so one source value feeds two response fields. (4) The request DTOs mark fields with @ApiProperty, but neither response class does, so API metadata is applied inconsistently.

violations.message: ChangeCuriersStatusDto.isActive is typed boolean but validated with @IsString(). This duplicates the wrong isActive check in UpdateCuriersInfoDto and breaks the module's @IsBoolean convention.
UpdateCuriersInfoDto.isActive is typed boolean but validated with @IsString(). The isActive check is copied here instead of being defined once and correctly.
fromDomain builds a SavedCurierOrderResponseDto but returns orderReadonly (the domain export) instead, skipping the module's own response DTO. It also maps commissionRate into paymentDetails.
